key_insight: In CaBi2B2O9 (B = Ta, Nb), ferroelectricity comes from a trilinear coupling of a polar mode with oxygen-octahedral rotations/tilts, while interlayer sliding between Bi2O2 and perovskite blocks is the core structural driver of polarization.
engineering_relevance: This work identifies design rules for layered ferroelectrics with high Curie temperature, strong anisotropic piezoelectric response, and intrinsically high resistivity—useful for robust oxide devices.
method: Group-theoretic mode analysis of symmetry breaking pathways
First-principles calculations of phase stability, polarization, and piezoelectric response
Comparison of Ta- and Nb-based Aurivillius compounds
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a combined theoretical evaluation showing that the A2_1am phase is stabilized by Γ5−X2+X3− trilinear coupling and that Bi ions and octahedral distortions dominate the computed polarization and piezoelectricity.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on theory and first-principles modeling, so experimental validation of the predicted interlayer-sliding mechanism and property magnitudes is still important.
paper_title: The origin of ferroelectricity, polarization and high resistivity in Aurivillius CaBi2B2O9 (B = Ta, Nb)
